title: CLR/19/2012 of RAJEEV BHATT/SHARMA and ANOTHER Vs YOGENDRA SINGH NEGI

paras.text:
CLR No.19 of 2012
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Mr Devesh Ghildiyal, Advocate for the
revisionist.
 Mr Piyush Garg, Advocate for the
respondent.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
 This revision has been preferred by the
revisionist against the order dated 02.03.2012
passed by the Judge, Small Cause
Court/Additional District Judge, Rishikesh
Dehradun in Small Cause Case No.18 of 2009 by
which the application of the defendant/revisionist
for amendment in written statement has been
rejected.
 The Small Cause Case No.18 of 2009 was
instituted in the year 09.07.2009. Written
statement was also filed by the defendant/
revisionist on 08.04.2011. During the pendency
of the suit the plaintiff/respondent filed few
documents alongwith examination in chief. The
defendant/revisionist moved an application for
amendment in written statement on the ground
that since the plaintiff/respondent has filed these
documents for the rebuttal of the same, the
amendment in the written statement is necessary.
The learned court below considered the
application of the defendant/revisionist and
rejected the same stating therein that whatever
documents have been filed by the
plaintiff/respondent, revisionist can file his own
documents in rebuttal. It is further mentioned in
the order that the proposed amendment sought in
the written statement is already there in the
written statement submitted by the
defendant/revisionist.

Learned counsel for the
defendant/revisionist submitted that the
revisionist, after denial of the amendment in the
written statement, will not get an opportunity to
rebut the document. He further submitted that
infact pleadings are also necessary for specific
denial of document in the written statement.
 On the other hand, Mr Piyush Garg,
Advocate for the respondent submitted that infact
pleadings are already given in the written
statement. In support of his submission he
referred paragraph 3, 5 & 9 of the plaint as well
as paragraph 3, 5 & 9 of the written statement.
He submitted that from the reading of these
paragraphs, it is clear that no further pleading is
required. He also submitted that several
opportunities were given to the
defendant/revisionist for cross-examination and
in such circumstances learned trial court has
rightly rejected the application of the
defendant/revisionist.
 I have considered the submissions of
learned counsel for the parties. I have also seen
the paragraphs 3, 5 & 9 of the plaint as well as
written statement. I am convinced that the points
which defendant/revisionist wants to submit in
his written statement by way of amendment are
already there in his written statement. As far as
rebuttal of documents filed by the
plaintiff/respondent is concerned, the
defendant/revisionist can also file documents in
rebuttal. I do not find any illegality in the order
passed by the trial court.
 Civil Revision is dismissed. Stay
application no.2800 of 2012 stands dispose of.
